articles.title: France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking
articles.summary: Fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets across France were affected last month [Getty Images] France has accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of being behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers across the country last month. Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said the attack was "unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression", adding those who were responsible would be hit with sanctions. Iran has yet to respond officially, but some Iranian media outlets have dismissed the allegations as baseless. The French hacking, which led to the destruction of tons of frozen anc chilled food in France was followed by a similar attack against supermarkets across several other European countries. It is not known if the instances are linked. Barrot said the attack on France's supermarkets "marks the first large-scale cyber-attack aimed at sabotage on our national territory, and it constitutes a major attack on the nation's interests and the security of the French people". He said the government had summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris to "lodge a very strong protest against this extremely grave act". France will take "any other necessary and proportionate measures" to respond to the incident and "deter anyone who might seek to repeat it", Barrot added. The Paris prosecutor said an investigation had been opened into the head of an offensive cyber unit associated with the IRGC as well as his two deputies. Laure Beccuau named the unit as Shahid Kaveh, which she said had an affiliation with the electronic and cyber centre of the IRGC. Shahid Kaveh is the name given to a cluster of hackers thought to be directly employed by the Iranian regime. In recent weeks, a number of commentators and politicians in Iran have argued that the country should extend any retaliation beyond the Middle East if the US and Israel resume the war they started earlier this year. If the IRGC carried out the cyber-attacks, it remains unclear whether they were part of Iran's deterrence strategy. On 11 October, hackers gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units used in many of France's supermarkets. More than 100 of Coopérative U's supermarkets were hit, as well as 180 stores from Intermarché and its Netto brand. In some stores, temperatures of the fridges reportedly rose to 50C (120F) overnight. Other major food retailers including Carrefour, Monoprix and E.Leclerc were also hit by the attack, which targeted software provided by Danish engineering firm Danfoss. The software allows retailers to manage their cold units remotely. Earlier this month a second wave of hacks took place, hitting more than 100 stores across Europe. Supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while a smaller number of shops were hit in countries including Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland. Separately in August a small number of US military bases had fridges mysteriously malfunction, spoiling food. This incident is also being investigated as deliberate cyber-attacks, Reuters news agency has reported, citing sources familiar with the matter. Since the waves of attacks on freezers, experts have been speculating which hacking groups could be responsible, with Iran being on a list of potential suspects. In spite of a pair of Russian-aligned hacktivist groups claiming they were responsible on Wednesday, few believed them. The French government has not said how it reached the conclusion that Iran was responsible, and attribution of cyber-attacks is extremely hard as hackers are able to hide their locations. Additional reporting by Farshad Bayan, BBC Persian. articles.title: GOP Rep. Massie introduces articles of impeachment against Pete Hegseth
articles.summary: Republican Rep. Thomas Massie introduced articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on the House floor Monday afternoon. House TV - PHOTO: Rep. Thomas Massie speaks on the House floor introducing articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in Washington, Nov. 9, 2026. Hegseth said on Monday that he's "not worried about" efforts to impeach him over his controversial leadership at the Pentagon and role administering the Iran war, announcing a rare press conference on the topic set for Tuesday. "We’re not worried about that,” Hegseth said when asked by a reporter about Republican support on Capitol Hill amid the impeachment effort led by outgoing Rep. Massie. "We're going to do a press conference tomorrow morning at the Pentagon on that very topic. So I'll save my remarks there. I hope you all come loaded for bear with your questions," said Hegseth, who hasn't held a press conference since May. Hegseth's comments came the same day Massie reintroduced a privileged resolution to impeach Hegseth. Calls to impeach Hegseth have grown as several Republicans have attributed the GOP's sweeping midterm losses to the Iran war. Trump dismisses prospect of replacing Hegseth amid Iran war fallout, looming Democratic investigations Massie went through the process in mid-September only to be thwarted by Speaker Mike Johnson, who canceled the final scheduled day of legislative business before the midterm elections -- staving off a vote at the time. "Here's the parliamentary reality of it. What Speaker Johnson has done, I believe, after talking to the parliamentarian, is I will have to refile the articles of impeachment when we get back,” Massie told ABC News on Sept. 16. "They will expire. Maybe they'll grow. Maybe he'll do something between now and the election that warrants another article, or and so I'll have to refile those when we get back." Carolyn Kaster/AP Photo - PHOTO: Rep. Thomas Massie speaks after losing the Republican party's nomination during an election night watch party at the Marriott Cincinnati Airport, May 19, 2026, in Hebron, Ky. After Massie's reintroduction of the resolution, the House must take up the measure within two legislative days -- forcing Republicans to go on the record defending Hegseth after suffering major losses in the 2026 midterm elections. Massie, a conservative who has gained a reputation as a constitutionalist through his seven terms in the House, lost a primary earlier this summer after President Donald Trump endorsed his opponent. Annabelle Gordon/POOL/EPA/Shutterstock - PHOTO: Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth in the Oval Office of the White House in Washington, DC, October 30, 2026. It's unclear whether an impeachment effort will succeed in the House, which is still under Republican control, but Massie told ABC News’ Jon Karl that he's confident there will be enough GOP defectors for it to pass. Massie needs a simple majority for the impeachment resolution to succeed in the House, meaning that just three Republicans need to vote with all Democrats to prevail. It doesn't appear that any Democrats will vote against the impeachment effort. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries came out in support of impeaching Hegseth saying on ABC News' "This Week" on Sunday that he's a "hard yes." GOP leaders could offer a motion to "table" the resolution rather than take a direct vote on the underlying measure. That would need to pass by a simple majority. House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer declined to back the Hegseth impeachment effort, but Massie volunteered that "there’s a lot of questions about" Hegseth, including the embattled secretary’s strategy in Iran. "I will weigh the debate and make a decision," retiring Republican Rep. Don Bacon told ABC News' Kyra Phillips on Friday when asked if he will vote to impeach Hegseth. "I do think the secretary has made some bad mistakes." Even if the measure passes in the House, it would still need approval by a two-thirds majority in the GOP-controlled Senate, a lofty threshold that's unlikely to be met. Congress returns for crowded lame-duck session as Hegseth impeachment, government funding deadline loom Trump has maintained that he has "every intention to keep" Hegseth atop the Pentagon. In a video posted Thursday, Hegseth proclaimed that he will not back down -- doubling down on the Iran war and his cultural agenda at the Pentagon while drawing a parallel to Trump. "This is not about me, but of course the other side, they’re obsessed. A disgruntled, defeated congressman, along with all his Democratic allies has also dropped sham articles of impeachment against yours truly. Just like they tried against President Trump twice," Hegseth said in the video. ABC News' Steven Beynon contributed to this report. articles.title: Russell Brand sentenced to more than 10 years in prison for rape and sexual assaults
articles.summary: The British former comedian and actor Russell Brand has been sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison for raping a woman and sexually assaulting three more. Handing down the sentence Monday at Southwark Crown Court in London, judge Joel Bennathan said Brand told a series of lies throughout the trial, adding he had displayed a "casual and arrogant disregard" for women who said 'No' to him. "About 20 years ago, Russell Brand, you were becoming famous," Bennathan said. "You were clever — and in many people's eyes, funny and charismatic. You had also become a sexual predator." He added, "Whatever women wear, wherever they go, indeed whatever they drink, they retain the right to say 'no' and to demand justice from criminal courts when sexual predators like you, Russell Brand, act without their consent." Brand was supported in court by his wife, Laura Gallacher, and his father, Ron. He is expected to serve at least two-thirds of that sentence — around seven years — before being eligible for release. Brand was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault on Nov. 5. He was acquitted of two rape counts and one count of attempted indecent assault. Prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones called Brand a ruthless, calculating, manipulative "sexual predator" who treated women as a "disposable commodity." "Mr. Brand abused the influence and power that came with his fame," Karmy-Jones said. "He used it to facilitate an access to women without which the offending could not have taken place. It also fed his own view that he could commit such offenses with impunity." Ahead of his sentencing, one woman, who was sexually assaulted by Brand in 2004 or 2005, told the court Monday in her impact statement: "Russell Brand is a sexual predator who has no remorse," Sky News reported. Another woman, who was raped by the comedian in 2009 after meeting him at a comedy show in London, said she was "living with trauma." She said his fame made it "difficult to escape reminders of what had happened," Reuters reported. She said she was worried after the attack that she might have HIV, struggled to eat and sleep, took two to three months off work and abandoned the career she had embarked upon. "Although the rape was 17 years ago, she still finds it affects her ability to form new friendships and to know when she can trust people," the judge said. A third woman who was assaulted by Brand while working on a Channel 4 documentary said that, following the attack, she felt like she had "lost my trust in people." Reflecting on the incident, she added: "I felt powerless in that moment." Last week, Megyn Kelly, the former Fox News host, reacted to Brand’s conviction in disbelief. “I don’t believe the charges, and I don’t have to believe them just because a jury came through with the opposite conclusion,” she said in a YouTube livestream . The next day, in a comment on X, Elon Musk described Brand’s conviction for offenses nearly 20 years old as a “ crazy legal standard .”  England doesn’t have a statute of limitations for rape or sexual assault. Brand became a household name in the U.K. in the 2000s as a comedian and broadcaster and had well-documented issues with drugs and alcohol. He went on to star in the movies Get Him to the Greek in 2010 and Arthur the following year. He married singer Katy Perry in October 2010, but Brand filed for divorce in December 2011, citing irreconcilable differences. Their divorce was finalized in July 2012. The claims against Brand were made by six different women, spanning from 1999 to 2009. None of the women knew each other, but came forward to police following a TV documentary and press reports in 2023, in which anonymous allegations were made by other women. Laura Brand, the wife of British actor and comedian Russell Brand, arrives at Southwark Crown Court Monday. REUTERS / REUTERS During the trial, the court heard tearful testimony from the six accusers, who are all entitled to lifelong anonymity. According to the Associated Press, the convictions included a rape that took place in 2009, involving a woman who went to Brand's home after meeting him at one of his shows. She said she had engaged in consensual sex, but that Brand then raped her and removed a condom in the process. Brand was also convicted of sexually assaulting a woman when he grabbed her breasts at a London bar in 2004. He was also found guilty over an incident in 2009, in which he demanded a woman give him a massage in front of two of his colleagues and then put his head in her groin. A third complaint of sexual assault ended in a guilty verdict when Brand was found guilty of pushing a woman who worked at a radio station up against a wall and forcibly kissing her. Brand denied the charges and said he had never forced anyone to do something against their will. Footage released by London's Metropolitan Police after the verdict shows Brand being interviewed by police in December 2023. "As I've repeatedly stated publicly and written about extensively, I led a very promiscuous life in the past, which I've spent years openly denouncing," Brand can be seen saying. "I've never engaged in non-consensual sexual activity." He said he did "not recall the names" of the complainants, or meeting them, adding, "However, it's entirely possible that I may have encountered them and we may have engaged in consensual sexual activity or physical contact that's been since reimagined." Following the verdict, London's Metropolitan Police Service told Yahoo News that Brand, 51, was facing further allegations of rape from two women. "The suspect has previously been interviewed under caution in connection with the allegations," the force said. Brand has not been charged in relation to these claims. The head of the Met Police, Sir Mark Rowley, has urged any other victims of Brand to contact the police.  "There's two more rape allegations that we're looking at. We're encouraging anybody else to come forward if there's any other allegations," he told British media on Nov. 6. He later said that he "wouldn't be surprised if many, many more come forward," adding of the trial, "This shows that powerful people can be brought down so you are safe stepping forward and we will support and try and bring that person to justice." articles.title: Nvidia CEO's affair has sparked a spy investigation. The stakes go beyond AI.
articles.summary: Nvidia's board of directors said Sunday it was launching an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang being the target of an alleged Chinese spy, with whom he had an affair. Huang admitted to the affair in an email to Nvidia employees and is cooperating with the investigation. Reports have identified Alice Huang (no relation), former executive at tech firm Megaspeed, as the person he had the relationship with. "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry," Jensen Huang said in a statement. If you haven't been following the stock market closely, you may not be familiar with Nvidia, one of the world's most valuable companies. And you may be wondering why U.S. security officials would be concerned about a CEO's extramarital affair. Here's what we know so far, and why this tech CEO's affair is a big deal. First, who is Jensen Huang? Jensen Huang is the CEO of Nvidia, one of the biggest makers of specialized computer chips in the world. Its chips were initially designed for computer graphics, but with the AI boom of the past few years, demand for Nvidia's hardware has skyrocketed. China and the U.S. are in a heated competition for AI technology, and that includes access to chips like the ones Nvidia makes. Jensen Huang is an American citizen who was born in Taiwan. He founded Nvidia in 1993 and has been the company's president and CEO since, steering the company through the AI boom of the past several years. What we know about the affair so far According to the New York Times, it's unclear when Jensen Huang met Alice Huang — an alleged Chinese spy — but the two were photographed together in 2024 at a bar in Taipei, Taiwan. It was roughly around that time when Megaspeed, the AI company she worked for, began its push into the AI sector. Multiple news reports were unable to confirm if Alice Huang is still employed at Megaspeed today. Megaspeed has touted its membership in Nvidia's partnership program, which would provide access to its latest technology. Huang apologized for the affair in a message to Nvidia employees, and asked for privacy for his family. "I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused," Huang wrote, "and I accept the criticism that comes with it." He pledged to earn back his employees' confidence, and added that he was cooperating fully with the board's investigation. "I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security," he wrote. The New York Times reported that U.S. intelligence officials believe Alice Huang was gathering information for the Chinese government. China denied that it was spying , calling the allegation unsubstantiated. "It is nothing but smears against China," a Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson said. The New York Times also reported that executives at Nvidia contacted the U.S. Commerce Department last year seeking information about the department's investigation into Megaspeed. The investigation was later transferred to the Department of Justice, which is reportedly looking into Megaspeed's involvement in potentially illegally routing Nvidia products into China. Why this matters AI is the biggest thing in tech right now, infiltrating our lives via chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude, and disrupting all sorts of industries from software development and bioengineering. Governments are trying to determine how and when to use AI for security and across business sectors too. China and the U.S. are hastily competing to dominate AI development for uses across multiple industries. The development has been so rapid that some CEOs of AI companies have suggested a pause may be in order before the technology develops beyond what humans can control. Nvidia has contracts with the U.S. government to use its technology in several areas , and Jensen Huang has a close relationship with President Trump. U.S. officials are trying to determine if the affair may have allowed the Chinese government to receive information about Nvidia's technology and its agreements with the U.S. government. Nvidia's board said in its statement that the company does not believe national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised. President Trump said late Sunday that he considers Huang "a fine person" who should stay on as CEO of Nvidia. "I think he probably has an excuse for it. We'll have to hear it," Trump told reporters Sunday night. "He's done an amazing job for our country." articles.title: Trump questions midterm results days after congratulating Democrats
articles.summary: President Donald Trump speaks with reporters before boarding Air Force One, at President Donald J. Trump International Airport in West Palm Beach, Florida, on Nov. 8, 2026. —Jaquelyn Martin—AP President Donald Trump questioned the integrity of the midterm elections on Monday, less than a week after the Republican Party suffered historic defeats in both swing states and former GOP strongholds . “Does anybody really believe that this ‘Election’ was honest,” Trump asked in a Truth Social post early Monday. “How could the Polls be so wrong???” “Some early voting ‘dumps’ were so large that it was impossible to win, no matter how many people went to vote,” he continued, adding: “It’s all about the machines, which are far more important than the voter!” His post did not elaborate on what was meant by the statement. Read more: Welcome to Trump’s Lame-Duck Era Trump’s unsubstantiated fraud claims come nearly two weeks after he told reporters on Oct. 27 that he would respect the election results “if they’re honest elections.” As results came in throughout Nov. 3 and into Nov. 4, Trump seemed to accept the outcome. “My message is, congratulations to the Democrats, and I look forward to working with you for the good of our country,” Trump told CBS News in an election-night phone call. It was a sentiment he repeated in an interview that aired Sunday on 60 Minutes , when he said he would be willing to work with Democrats on immigration, addressing an issue that had been top-of-mind for voters ahead of Election Day. “I think that's something that's actually doable," he said. By Monday morning, however, Trump was casting doubt on the results. The comment harkens back to Trump’s unsubstantiated claims of election interference and ensuing lawsuits after he lost the presidency to Joe Biden in 2020. Trump's history of election denial Trump was sowing doubt on the 2020 election before voting began, telling the public that August that “the only way we’re going to lose this election is if the election is rigged.” Following his loss, Trump refused to concede to Biden. Instead, he began to spread conspiracy theories about widespread election fraud, without evidence. On Nov. 7, 2020, shortly before news organizations projected Biden’s victory, Trump falsely declared on Twitter that he had “WON THIS ELECTION, BY A LOT!” Echoing Trump’s false claims also became a test of loyalty within the Republican Party, with House Speaker Mike Johnson, Ohio Rep. Jim Jordan, and former Georgia Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene among those who espoused the false view. Trump and his allies filed 62 lawsuits challenging or seeking to overturn the results between Nov. 4, 2020, and Jan. 6, 2021, according to the House Jan. 6 committee . Only one produced a victory—a narrow Pennsylvania ruling that didn’t establish fraud or change the outcome. Some cases were dismissed on procedural grounds; others failed on the merits. The legal defeats did not stop Trump from repeating his false claims. On Dec. 22, 2020, he alleged on social media that Democrats had “DUMPED HUNDREDS OF THOUSANDS OF BALLOTS IN THE SWING STATES LATE IN THE EVENING.” The claims escalated on Jan. 5, 2021, when Trump tweeted : “Washington is being inundated with people who don’t want to see an election victory stolen by emboldened Radical Left Democrats.” This followed repeated calls for his supporters to descend upon Washington D.C. and protest the results . As Congress met to count and certify the Electoral College votes on Jan. 6, 2021, a mob of Trump supporters stormed the U.S. Capitol. His efforts to overturn his 2020 defeat also led to criminal charges. In August 2023, Special Counsel Jack Smith brought four federal charges against Trump, alleging efforts to subvert the results through pressure on officials, fraudulent elector slates, and interference with certification. Trump pleaded not guilty. On the campaign trail in 2024, he doubled down on his allegations of election interference by urging voters to deliver a victory that was “too big to rig.” The case was dismissed in November that year, after his reelection, because of Justice Department policy against prosecuting a sitting President. articles.title: The James Gunn-Peter Safran era of DC Studios is over after 4 years
articles.summary: James Gunn and Peter Safran are out at DC Studios, with Jeremy Latcham taking over (Credit: Getty Images) After four years at DC Studios, James Gunn and Peter Safran will not be leading the company through its next chapter under Skydance ownership as they are handing the reins over to new president and chief creative officer Jeremy Latcham. In a statement, the two executives spoke with pride of their work at the studio and gave Latcham, who worked with Gunn on the “Guardians of the Galaxy” trilogy at Marvel Studios, their blessing. Skydance says that the duo will “return full time to their creative work,” which includes post-production on the “Superman” sequel “Man of Tomorrow” and work on other DC projects. “Four years ago, we set out to unite DC under one creative vision. In that time, we helped restore ‘Superman’ to the heart of DC, while opening new doors and telling new stories in film and television with ‘Peacemaker’, ‘Creature Commandos,’ ‘Lanterns’ and ‘Clayface . ‘ We’re immensely proud of the team that turned that ambition into something real, including the actors, crews and executives we had the opportunity to collaborate with,” Gunn and Safran said. “We’ve shared a creative history with Jeremy going back to Marvel, and we’re eager to see the perspective he brings to DC’s next chapter. We’re excited to return to what drew us to this job in the first place, which is telling the stories we love, including the next chapter of Clark and Lex’s journey in ‘Man of Tomorrow,’” the duo said. Jeremy Latcham DC Studios Latcham was part of the founding core of Marvel Studios under Kevin Feige and worked on global blockbusters like “Iron Man,” “The Avengers,” and Tom Holland’s “Spider-Man” films. Latcham will lead DC’s film, television and animation slate, overseeing the creative pipeline, along with production, talent and strategy. Latcham, who will begin at DC on Dec. 1, will report to Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein, co-chairs of Skydance Motion Picture Group. “Jeremy brings a deep reverence for DC and its passionate fanbase, recognizing that they are the very foundation of this storied, multigenerational brand,” said Goldberg and Greenstein. “Under his leadership, every film and television show will be ushered from start to finish through the prism of the legions of fans who love and champion it. Jeremy’s track record exemplifies the excellence he will bring to building out DC and the many beloved characters within it.” “DC’s pantheon of characters is among the most iconic in American popular culture. I’ve had the privilege to help bring some of the most celebrated superhero stories to life on the big screen, and I’m excited and honored for the opportunity to now lead DC Studios into its next era. The chance to steward the incredible cast of DC characters to the screen in a way that excites lifelong fans while introducing their timeless stories to the next generation is a massive responsibility that I do not take lightly,” said Latcham. Gunn and Safran have released three theatrical films since taking over DC Studios, starting with “Superman,” which grossed $618 million worldwide amid strong reviews. But the studio’s follow-up, “Supergirl,” fell flat this past summer, earning just $126.4 million globally. The more modestly budgeted “Batman” villain horror film “Clayface” has fared better, grossing $109 million through its first three weekends in theaters. On the TV side, Gunn and Safran developed hit shows like the John Cena-led “Suicide Squad” spinoff “Peacemaker” and the animated show “Creature Commandos,” as well as the recent hit show “Lanterns.” “James and Peter launched a new era for DC Studios and led it through a period of real transformation, resetting the foundation and building a slate we’re incredibly proud of. We’re grateful for their passion, contributions and commitment to this legendary brand,” David Ellison, chairman and CEO, and Ynon Kreiz, co-CEO, of Skydance said in a statement. “Jeremy has been a longtime creative partner to both, and we have complete confidence that James and Peter will ensure a smooth, collaborative transition and continue this work with care. We look forward to working with Jeremy to build the next generation of DC storytelling and to doubling down on our commitment to fans,” Ellison and Kreiz added. articles.title: Ole Miss investigating 'deeply troubling' video of racist gestures
articles.summary: The University of Mississippi launched an investigation after a video purportedly showing students making racist gestures on another student's doorbell camera was shared on social media. The video shows two girls making monkey sounds and gestures as they pass by a Ring camera on an apartment door. The person who posted it said her daughter's doorbell camera captured it and that her daughter is a freshman at Ole Miss and has two Black roommates, CBS affiliate WREG reported. A university spokesperson told CBS News that it condemned the "offensive, hurtful, and unacceptable behaviors" depicted in the video and that the appropriate university offices and processes are actively investigating the incident. "It's important to note that student conduct cases, records and any potential disciplinary action are protected by the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA)," the statement said. "We are committed to maintaining a safe and welcoming environment for all of our students, faculty, staff, and visitors and will follow our processes to ensure the well-being and safety of our community." In a subsequent statement to students, faculty and staff, the vice chancellor of student affairs condemned the behavior depicted in the video and said that it "does not reflect our university's values or the kind of community we strive to be every day." "The behavior depicted in this video is deeply troubling, hurtful, and unacceptable," Shawnboda Mead said in a statement posted on the university's website . Mead said staff have reached out to the students directly impacted and will continue to support them through the process. She also recognized that situations like this can cause "hurt and concern" among students and assured that the matter is "being taken seriously." Mead also urged people to be thoughtful about the information being shared online as one student has already been incorrectly identified as being involved in this incident. She said, despite online rumors, no members of the university's sorority community were involved in the incident. "Every student deserves to feel safe, respected, and valued at the University of Mississippi," Mead said. "Racism and actions that disparage people because of an aspect of their identity have no place in our campus community." articles.title: Biden says Trump's Jan. 6 actions 'should follow him to his grave'
articles.summary: Former President Joe Biden also wrote in his memoir that Trump 'led an insurrection.'  (Brent Stirton / Getty) Former President Joe Biden issued scathing criticism of President Donald Trump in his forthcoming memoir, saying his actions during the Jan. 6, 2021, attack on the Capitol “should follow him to his grave.” Biden’s comments, published as a book excerpt in The Atlantic on Monday, mark some of his strongest criticism of Trump since the former president left office. In the excerpt, Biden says Trump “led an insurrection” and slammed his decision to issue sweeping pardons of Jan. 6 defendants. Trump and Biden at Trump's inauguration ceremony at the Capitol in 2025. (Chip Somodevilla / Getty) “The criminals who attacked law-enforcement officers that day didn’t deserve pardons,” Biden wrote. “They deserved prison terms.” The former president added that Trump and the president’s supporters “continue to preen and posture like they’re supporters of law enforcement.” “Here’s my view: You don’t get to turn a blind eye to cops being punched, speared, sprayed, and brutalized and call yourself a friend of law enforcement,” he wrote. “What Trump did on January 6, 2021, should never be forgotten. It should follow him to his grave.” Reached for comment, White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis called Biden “the worst president in American history.” She pointed to his handling of the border, crime and inflation, adding, “What they did to this country should never be forgotten.” The memoir, “Promise Me, America,” is set to be published on Nov. 17. In a September interview with Time magazine, Trump acknowledged that he was considering pardoning members of his administration before his term concluded, pointing to Biden’s decision to issue preemptive pardons. Biden issued those pardons to his son, Hunter Biden , and other members of his family, lawmakers on the congressional Jan. 6 committee, Dr. Anthony Fauci, and former Joint Chiefs of Staff Chairman Mark Milley. Biden also described his meeting with Trump after the 2024 election, part of a tradition where the outgoing president briefs the incoming president. Biden said that Trump’s tone “bordered on fawning” and said that Trump told him that “if it weren’t for politics, I believe we’d be good friends” — a remark that the former president said left him “too stunned to respond.” “He said my performance on job creation had been ‘extraordinary,’” Biden wrote. “He added that he’d been relieved he didn’t have to run against me. I didn’t really understand why he was buttering me up, so I cut off his compliments to move on to the business at hand.” During the approximately two hour meeting, Biden said that he wanted to give Trump an overview of world issues that he believed would “dominate his presidency.” “He nodded appreciatively,” Biden said of Trump. “But I noticed a curious pattern: He focused on the personalities of the leaders, as if we were sharing gossip about people at a dinner party, not discussing issues of global significance.” Biden announced Sunday that he would not “be able to do as many conversations about my book as I’d hoped,” pointing to his fight against cancer. “Some days are better than others,” Biden said in the post to X. “It hasn’t stopped me. But sometimes it slows me down.” This article was originally published on NBCNews.com This article originally appeared on NBC News at https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/joe-biden/memoir-trump-jan-6-2021-riot-follow-him-to-grave-2024-election-rcna608275

articles.title: Trump's hold on Senate Republicans faces a new test after election losses
articles.summary: Senate Republicans returning to the Capitol on Monday are furious with President Trump, whom they blame for last week's big losses in Senate and House races. The anger is raising the chances that the party could pivot away from the lame-duck president in the lead-up to the 2028 presidential election, according to GOP aides and strategists. Tensions are also rising with Trump’s Friday announcement that immigration hard-liner Stephen Miller will be his new chief of staff, replacing the outgoing Susie Wiles. The Miller appointment suggests a doubling down on the president’s policies, particularly on immigration enforcement, after an election in which Hispanic voters swung decisively toward Democrats, especially in Texas. Rep. Marlin Stutzman (R-Ind.) on Sunday said Miller should be fired, not promoted. “If your team takes a beating as badly as we took this last week, you have to fire people,” Stutzman said in an interview on CNN. “You don’t promote those who are — who were in charge of what was supposed to be delivered.” Whit Ayres, a prominent Republican pollster, said Senate Republicans will be less deferential to Trump after suffering a huge loss of seats in last week’s election. Ayres said Trump “clearly will remain the leader of the party for the next two years, but I also think the knee-jerk obeisance to whatever his whims are at the moment is likely over.” “There is so much resentment particularly among Republicans in the Senate for what Donald Trump did in North Carolina and South Carolina and Texas,” he said, referring to Trump’s endorsement of candidates Michael Whatley, Darline Graham and Ken Paxton, who all lost by large margins in the general election. “I think his iron grip over the Senate Republicans is likely to be loosened,” Ayres said. One senior Senate Republican aide predicted GOP senators and the broader party will begin to shift away from Trump over the next year. “Trump said he was on the ballot. He wasn’t on the ballot but acted like he was on the ballot,” and “a lot of people” voted as if Trump was atop the GOP ticket when they voted for Democrats in battleground states around the country, the aide said. “We need somebody who can work together with people, who doesn’t just try to divide — who is focused on real issues that people care about that are of importance versus stupid little internet memes, which it seems like Trump and Vance are more focused on now,” the aide argued. Republican sources say Trump undermined their chances of winning key Senate races by endorsing weak candidates, such as Paxton and Graham, and by failing to adhere to any message discipline. GOP senators are also frustrated by what they saw as Trump’s reluctance to spend from his massive campaign war chest until late in the campaign. Senate Republican aides and pollsters say Trump's dismal influence on races across the country will spark an intense discussion about what's next for the party and whether it's time to turn the page on MAGA and its policies. Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) and members of his leadership team lobbied Trump for months to back Sen. John Cornyn (R-Texas) over Paxton, the state attorney general, in the Texas Senate Republican primary — or to at least stay neutral — but Trump ignored their advice and endorsed Paxton before the primary runoff, sinking Cornyn’s chances. Thune and his leadership team urged the president and Senate GOP colleagues to keep their political messaging focused on their legislative accomplishments, especially the popular tax cuts in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, such as its tax deductions for tips. But Trump instead often veered off from the plan, getting into fights over the White House ballroom, the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, the Kennedy Center, the East Potomac Park golf course and other topics that GOP strategists viewed as unhelpful to delivering the broader Republican message. Trump blamed last week’s losses on poor Republican candidates, but many Senate Republicans think the blame for the loss of at least seven seats lies squarely with the unpopular president. “We’re up here talking about the generational benefits of avoiding a $4 trillion-plus tax hike and everything else that’s inside that bill, and then the president is talking about the Reflecting Pool or the ballroom, and those are the things that get the headlines,” a Senate GOP aide said. “Message synchronization was off.” Senate Republicans were galled when Trump dismissed the passage of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act as a “big yawn.” GOP leaders were touting the bipartisan legislation as a major accomplishment to address housing affordability, but Trump popped their balloon as he said he cared more about passing the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility (SAVE America) Act, a package to overhaul election rules that had virtually no chance of passing Congress. Senate Republican sources also said Trump waited too long to spend the hundreds of millions of dollars he stockpiled ahead of the midterm elections. “They sat on that $400 million until it was too late to start spending it,” a second GOP aide said. Trump said in August he would spend “a lot” of money from a pro-Trump super PAC to help “good” GOP candidates, but Senate GOP strategists complained the president’s political allies waited until the final weeks of the campaign to dump money into races, which diluted their firepower because they had to pay higher television ad rates. Trump announced in late October that he would end up spending more than $400 million by Election Day to help Republicans keep Congress. When Republicans got blown out on Election Day, the White House blamed GOP candidates for not putting in as much effort as the president to promote their candidacies and records. Trump declared on election night: “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” Senate Republicans say they think Trump also hurt them by constantly bashing their failure to pass the SAVE America Act, even after Republicans held at least five votes on the legislation, either in whole or in part, and came nowhere close to collecting the 60 votes the bill needed to advance. Trump warned Senate Republicans would be “in big trouble” if they didn’t abolish the filibuster to ram the bill through the chamber. “When you’re casting your own teammate as the opponent, what message does that send to the voter?” the GOP aide said. A third Senate Republican aide argued that Trump clearly deserves the blame for the loss of seven — and maybe as many as nine — Senate seats and more than 40 House seats. “Trump’s message was, ‘I’m going to deliver you a good economy,’ and it seems like the only person who benefited from the economy was him,” the aide said, adding that Democrats successfully tied together voters’ concerns about rising prices and corruption in Washington. “Those two things led to a disaster with independents,” the aide said. The GOP aide said some Senate Republicans expect more “pushback to Trump because his half-life is rapidly diminishing” but cautioned that “he’s still a popular figure in the Republican Party.” The president’s elevation of Miller, who is seen as a conservative hard-liner, may be a bid to keep base MAGA voters firmly in his corner. Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N.C.), one of Miller’s sharpest critics in the Senate GOP conference, called his elevation to chief of staff a “colossal mistake.” “The worst of all possible choices,” Tillis told CNN’s Jake Tapper. “The president needs to rethink it.” Senate Republican candidate John Sununu blamed Trump for his double-digit loss to Rep. Chris Pappas (D) in New Hampshire, a state that Senate GOP leaders in August saw as a promising opportunity to flip a Democratic-held seat. Sununu said Trump’s failure to end the months-long conflict with Iran and a steady stream of media stories about Trump’s family business dealings sunk his chances of winning. “This president ran and won on a platform of no more needless, endless wars. And then he attacked Iran, and we're still in it,” he told SiriusXM’s “The John Kasich Show.” “This president ran on and won on a platform of drain the swamp, right? … And now it seems like he or his family is in on every transaction and deal that goes on in Washington,” he said. “And those two things, I think, caused people to say, ‘You know, I just can't vote for a Republican while he's still in office.’” Cornyn argued Trump “misread his mandate” after the 2024 election. He argued the president’s “arbitrary” decisions on tariffs raised prices for millions of Americans without improving trade deals, and the administration’s “hyperaggressive” immigration enforcement efforts went well beyond what voters expected. “Voters wanted to retool our trading relationships, but got arbitrary ‘Liberation Day’ tariffs that raised prices without creating incentives for long-term reshoring. Voters wanted secure borders and peaceful streets, but got hyperaggressive immigration enforcement,” Cornyn wrote in a Wall Street Journal op-ed. Other Republicans have stepped up to defend Thune and Senate GOP leaders, arguing that they had little control over the negative political environment that Trump played a major role in creating. “I don’t think any rational, honest person … could blame John Thune for any of this,” Sen. Kevin Cramer (R-N.D.) told reporters shortly before the election. “I don’t think anybody could blame him for any bad outcome.” Asked if Trump would get most of the blame if Republicans lost control of the Senate, Cramer only said, “There will be a lot of finger-pointing.” Copyright 2026 Nexstar Media, Inc. articles.title: 11月10日会员早报：美国人失业担忧升至2020年4月以来最高 美国民主党想借12月11日大限逼停伊朗战争
articles.summary: 1、【美国人失业担忧升至2020年4月以来最高】纽约联储周一（11月9日）发布的10月消费者预期调查（SCE）显示，受访者认为一年后美国失业率将高于当前水平的平均概率升至45.3%，较9月上升1.4个百分点，为2020年4月以来最高；纽约联储称，升幅主要来自没有大学学历的受访者。2020年4月正是新冠疫情冲击最猛烈的时候。通胀预期没有变化，仍在高位。一年期、三年期和五年期通胀预期中值分别为3.9%、3.3%和3.0%，均与9月持平。 2、【美国民主党想借12月11日大限逼停伊朗战争】美国国会民主党人正在考虑，在12月11日政府临时拨款到期时，要求新的拨款法案写入“禁止将资金用于伊朗战争”的条款，否则就投票卡住法案，以此逼特朗普结束这场已打了八个多月、推高全球油价的战争。拨款法案在参议院需要60票才能通过，而共和党只有53席。如果双方僵持不下，联邦政府将在资金到期后停摆，这将是特朗普第二任期内的第四次停摆。民主党在11月3日的中期选举中赢得参众两院，但要到明年1月3日才正式接管国会。党内正在争论是现在就摊牌，还是等掌权后再动手，领导层还没有拍板。 3、【KKR季度利润创历史新高】美国另类资管巨头KKR周一（11月9日）公布2026年第三季度业绩，季度利润创下历史新高。衡量盈利能力的核心指标调整后净利润（ANI）同比增长29%，至16.5亿美元，合每股1.78美元，高于分析师平均预期（每股1.59美元）。KKR成立于1976年，是全球最大的私募股权机构之一。近年来，它已从传统并购基金发展为资产管理、保险、战略控股三大板块并行的综合性另类资管集团。 4、【乌克兰恢复空袭炼油厂，俄罗斯石油公司全国限购汽油】11月9日凌晨，俄罗斯第二大炼油厂遭到袭击。俄罗斯国有石油巨头、全国最大的石油生产商俄罗斯石油公司（Rosneft）在全国各地加油站重新实行限购。按照新规，城市加油站每车最多加30升，公路沿线最多50升。这次限售距Rosneft在10月23日取消上一轮限购还不到三周。 5、【英伟达股价重挫】英伟达周一盘中一度重挫8.8%，市值一度蒸发近4000亿美元，之后收复部分失地。英伟达董事会前一天表示，正在调查黄仁勋的婚外情关系，公司称，不认为有机密因此外泄。黄仁勋周日给全体员工写信，向家人和同事道歉，直言“我对妻子不忠”，并表示支持董事会调查、会全力配合。信里没有点名，但他已向董事会承认，对方是英伟达客户、新加坡数据中心公司Megaspeed的高管。

articles.title: Anthropic路演最快本周二启动，AI抛售潮后IPO定价迎大考
articles.summary: AI概念股上周遭遇剧烈抛售之际，Anthropic的重磅IPO即将进入正式路演阶段。这家AI行业明星最快将于本周二启动IPO营销，力争在美国感恩节前完成上市，但市场对AI资产的风险偏好已经发生变化，其发行定价和投资者认购需求将接受严峻考验。 上周AI产业链股票集体重挫后， 华尔街见闻 提到，上周五的报道称，部分潜在投资者讨论的Anthropic估值已降至约1.2万亿至1.3万亿美元，甚至有人考虑低至1.1万亿美元，较此前1.4万亿至1.5万亿美元的市场预期明显下调，更远低于早前市场讨论的最高约2万亿美元估值。 这意味着，Anthropic即将面对的不仅是能否完成一笔超大型IPO，更是公开市场愿意为前沿AI公司的增长潜力支付多高溢价。 等待期结束，最快周二启动路演，感恩节前上市仍是目标 Anthropic此次IPO的时间表正进入关键阶段。 据彭博社11月9日周一的报道，Anthropic最快可于11月10日开始正式IPO营销。根据美国证券交易委员会（SEC）的相关规定，公司公开提交IPO注册文件至少15个日历日后，才能正式启动面向投资者的营销活动。Anthropic于10月26日公开提交S-1招股书，因此本周二将迎来正式路演的最早时间窗口。 若进展顺利，Anthropic有望在11月16日当周完成定价并登陆纳斯达克，赶在11月26日美国感恩节假期前完成上市。Anthropic此前计划在纳斯达克全球精选市场上市，股票代码为ANT。 此次IPO的融资规模同样引人关注。彭博社报道称，Anthropic的目标是达到甚至超过SpaceX此前创纪录的IPO融资规模。SpaceX今年6月上市融资862亿美元，成为史上规模最大的IPO之一。路透社此前报道则称，Anthropic此次发行规模可能达到1000亿美元。 高盛和摩根士丹利担任此次IPO的牵头承销商，另有20家银行参与。不过，路演启动并不意味着发行条件已经敲定，最终发行价格区间、发行股数和融资规模仍需根据投资者反馈确定。 AI抛售冲击市场信心，IPO窗口能否维持成为关键 Anthropic此次IPO面临的挑战，不仅是投资者对公司自身估值的分歧，还有整个AI产业链风险偏好的变化。 本周一的报道指出，上周市场剧烈波动曾推动“恐慌指数”——芝加哥期权交易所的波动率指数（VIX）上周四升破25.00至28.00上方、收创3月末以来七个月新高。 Renaissance Capital高级策略师Matt Kennedy表示，VIX处于25以上水平时，企业通常会考虑推迟IPO。不过，Anthropic此次发行规模和投资故事都不同于一般IPO，市场环境对其上市计划的影响可能有所不同。 此前，上周AI股票遭遇集中抛售，纳斯达克100指数上周四跌超6%，指数成分股整体市值一日蒸发约2.3万亿美元。AI基础设施供应商、云计算企业及半导体公司均遭遇明显抛售，投资者开始重新评估AI资本开支的可持续性，以及数据中心建设能否产生足够回报。 除了市场波动，AI基础设施扩张还面临政治和监管层面的不确定性。美国中期选举后，民主党取得进展，引发市场对数据中心建设监管趋严的担忧。部分州限制数据中心开发的相关投票结果，也使AI企业未来获取算力和建设基础设施的难度受到关注。 不过，11月9日本周一，市场出现一定程度的修复。VIX盘中曾回落至约20.11，周一午盘时段，标普500指数涨超2%，费城半导体指数涨超6%。市场波动有所缓和，为Anthropic启动路演提供了相对有利的窗口。 Renaissance Capital的Kennedy认为，Anthropic的IPO可能不同于一般企业上市，最终关键在于发行定价能否获得市场认可。对于公司而言，当前市场环境未必足以迫使其推迟上市，但投资者对发行折价和估值的要求可能更高。 营收高速增长难掩盈利压力，投资者等待10月收入数据 估值争议的另一核心，是Anthropic能否证明自身的营收增长足以支撑如此庞大的上市估值。 根据公司11月2日向SEC提交的修订版招股书，Anthropic第三季度营收达到169.56亿美元，同比增长1127%，较第二季度增长约47%。今年前三季度累计营收达到332.42亿美元，企业客户扩张是重要推动力。 但增长速度已经出现放缓迹象。第二季度营收环比增长144%，第三季度环比增幅降至47%。尽管这一增速仍然相当可观，但对于一家潜在估值超过万亿美元的公司而言，投资者更关注增长能否持续，以及新增收入能否转化为利润。 第三季度，Anthropic经营亏损5.67亿美元，而第二季度曾实现9.74亿美元经营利润；净亏损达到232.91亿美元，较上年同期扩大约92%。公司解释称，第三季度经营业绩转亏主要受到约50亿美元短期算力采购成本，以及约20亿美元员工捐赠匹配计划相关非现金费用影响。 更令投资者关注的是，公司披露的计算能力采购及基础设施承诺支出总额达到8954亿美元，其中近一半预计在2030年底前兑现。巨额长期算力承诺意味着公司未来仍需要持续投入大量资本，也增加了业务增长和现金流之间的平衡难度。 路透社上周四的报道称，投资者还在等待Anthropic的10月营收数据。公司在更新后的招股书中尚未披露这一数字，部分投资者希望借此判断公司能否扭转近期增长放缓的趋势。 对于Anthropic而言，10月收入表现、企业客户使用量以及算力成本控制能力，都可能成为路演期间投资者重点追问的问题。 超大型IPO考验AI融资市场，Anthropic定价将影响行业估值 Anthropic此次IPO的意义并不局限于公司自身融资。 作为首批以开发前沿AI模型为核心业务、尝试登陆公开市场的公司之一，Anthropic的发行定价将为整个AI行业提供重要估值参照。尤其是在AI基础设施投资规模不断扩大、科技股估值遭遇重新审视之际，公开市场对Anthropic的认购热情，可能影响投资者对其他AI公司的估值判断。 如果Anthropic能够在市场波动后如期启动路演，并获得足够强劲的认购需求，将有望证明市场仍愿意为具备领先模型能力和商业化规模的AI公司提供巨额资本。反之，如果公司不得不大幅降低发行估值，甚至推迟上市，则可能进一步加剧市场对AI生态系统融资能力的担忧。 投资者的分歧反映出当前市场的两种判断：一方面，Claude等前沿模型的企业应用需求仍在快速增长，AI商业化空间远未被充分开发；另一方面，算力采购、数据中心建设和能源供应需要长期巨额投入，AI企业能否获得与投资规模相匹配的回报仍存在不确定性。 因此，Anthropic此次IPO真正的看点，已经不只是能否实现万亿美元级估值，而是经历AI概念股大幅调整后，公开市场究竟愿意为前沿AI公司的长期增长支付多少价格。 本周路演将给出第一个重要答案。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 美国民主党考虑以政府停摆为筹码，逼迫特朗普结束伊朗战争
articles.summary: 美国国会民主党人正在评估是否借助12月11日政府资金到期节点，向特朗普政府施压，迫使其终止对伊朗的战争行动。这一抉择不仅关乎政府能否正常运转，更将左右伊朗战争的走向及其对能源价格的持续冲击。 众议院拨款委员会首席民主党人Rosa DeLauro措辞强硬： "民主党绝不会为特朗普这场推高美国家庭生活成本、让美国更不安全的选择性战争提供资金。" 参议院拨款委员会首席民主党人Patty Murray亦表示， 民主党将动用一切可用手段终结这场战争。 民主党参议院领袖查克·舒默表示， 民主党将寻求通过"钱袋子权力"阻止战争，但未透露具体方案。 若民主党选择正面对抗，将触发特朗普第二任期内第四次完全或部分政府停摆，导致政府非必要职能暂停运转。然而，历史先例显示，停摆鲜少能够实现发起方的政策目标。 布伦特原油期货周一下跌4.7%，延续上周跌势。 两种路径：立即出手还是等待明年翻转国会 民主党眼下面临两条路径的抉择。 其一，在现任共和党掌控的国会"跛鸭会期"内立即采取行动，借助资金悬崖向特朗普施压，尽快结束战争、缓解汽油和柴油等能源价格压力； 其二，按兵不动，等待明年中期选举大胜的成果落地——届时民主党将同时翻转众参两院多数席位，届时在立法层面将拥有更大主动权。 这一战略并非没有历史依据。民主党正在研究上世纪70年代国会通过拨款程序迫使越战结束时所使用的立法语言，试图复制这一路径。 进步派参议员Chris Van Hollen明确呼吁，民主党应在下一个支出法案中封锁战争资金，他援引历史称："越战的终结，正是因为国会切断了军费。" 停摆筹码的局限性：历史先例并不乐观 尽管进步派呼声高涨，民主党领袖层对于重蹈停摆覆辙明显存有顾虑。 近年来的历史表明，停摆作为政策杠杆的效果相当有限。 民主党2025年下半年持续43天的必要支出法案封锁，以争取延续《平价医疗法案》保费补贴为目标，最终政府资金恢复时这一目标并未实现。 2013年共和党发起的长达16天停摆试图削减《平价医疗法案》资金，同样以失败告终。 此外，停摆期间，被认定为必要岗位的政府雇员须无薪工作，非必要政府职能全面暂停，对普通民众的直接冲击可能反噬发起方的政治声望。 多条战线：债务上限与国防预算成潜在筹码 即便放弃停摆路线，民主党仍握有其他若干手段。 在今年年底前， 参议院若干必须通过的立法事项仍需至少部分民主党票数以绕过冗长辩论程序。 其中，一项必须通过的国防政策授权法案需要在12月内完成，而特朗普政府申请的用于资助伊朗行动的紧急补充拨款，目前在共和党掌控的参议院遭到搁置。 明年掌握多数后，民主党还可将债务上限谈判作为筹码——前提是共和党今年未能通过无法被冗长辩论阻拦的特殊预算程序提前上调上限。 目前已有讨论认为，共和党可能借助五角大楼预算法案将40万亿美元债务上限捆绑上调，以剥夺民主党未来的谈判筹码，但国会山迄今未见共和党领袖积极推动这一方案的迹象。 与此同时，五角大楼正寻求通过党派预算程序追加至少3500亿美元，若这一需求最终留待民主党掌控的国会明年处理，将为双方就整体可支配支出水平及伊朗战争问题展开谈判创造新的空间。 跛鸭会期多线并行：能源许可、司法提名与弹劾风险 伊朗战争资金争议之外，本届跛鸭国会还需处理多项未竟事务。 本周参议院将就一项旨在简化能源项目许可审批的两党法案进行表决，该法案覆盖可再生能源与化石燃料项目，但众议院民主党领袖对其环境影响存有疑虑，可能在众院层面予以阻拦。 华盛顿同时高度警惕最高法院法官退休或内阁出缺的可能性，任何此类变动都将触发在共和党参议院于1月3日结束前赶完确认程序的紧迫压力。 此外，共和党众议员Thomas Massie提出弹劾国防部长Pete Hegseth的动议，一旦推进，将大量占用本已紧张的国会议事时间。 共和党参议院领袖则抓紧时间，力图在参议院多数权易手前批准尽可能多的特朗普司法提名人选。多条政治议程相互交织，令这一跛鸭会期的走向充满变数。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 纽约联储调查：美国消费者通胀预期稳定，失业率担忧升至2020年以来最高
articles.summary: 美国消费者对未来一年通胀预期保持稳定，但对劳动力市场的悲观情绪明显升温，折射出当前经济前景的内在矛盾。 纽约联储周一发布的月度消费者预期调查显示， 受访者对未来一年通胀的预期维持在3.9%，三年及五年通胀预期亦分别稳定在3.3%和3%。 与此同时，消费者对失业率上升的预期概率攀升至2020年4月以来最高水平，折射出民众对就业市场的隐忧。 通胀预期总体平稳，但就业前景的分歧将为美联储的政策路径提供重要参考。 多位美联储官员近期表示，需要通过渐进式加息将通胀压回2%的政策目标，10月消费者价格指数（CPI）数据将于周二公布，届时或进一步左右市场对货币政策走向的判断。 失业率担忧升至四年半高位，内部分化明显 纽约联储调查显示， 受访者预计未来一年失业率将上升的平均概率升至45.3%，为2020年4月以来最高，主要由无大学学历的受访者推动。 然而，该调查同时呈现出相反的信号：在已失业人群中，找到新工作的概率连续第二个月改善，达到2025年11月以来的最高水平。 对于在职人员，未来一年失去工作的概率小幅上升，但主动辞职的意愿有所下降，与 美联储官员所描述的"低解雇、低招聘"环境相吻合。 美联储官员曾多次表示，当前劳动力市场处于微妙平衡之中。10月政府就业报告显示，失业率降至4.1%，非农新增就业好于预期，表明市场仍具韧性。 个人财务状况喜忧参半 在个人财务层面，纽约联储数据同样呈现出分化格局。 未来三个月内无法偿还最低债务的概率升至去年12月以来最高水平，反映出部分消费者的还款压力有所加剧；与此同时，信贷获取的感知状况变化不大。 在财务状况的主观评价上， 认为过去一年财务状况有所改善的家庭比例略有上升，但预计未来一年财务状况将恶化的受访者比例也小幅走高，两种情绪并存。 此前公布的数据显示，截至9月的季度美国经济增速达到近一年最快水平，其他多项调查也显示，消费者对个人财务前景的信心有所回暖，与此次调查中的部分悲观信号形成对照。 通胀预期锚定，加息路径仍存分歧 消费者通胀预期的总体稳定，为美联储政策制定提供了一定的操作空间。 上月，美联储将联邦基金利率目标区间维持在3.75%至4%不变，但多位官员此后表示，渐进式加息仍有必要，以引导通胀回落至2%的长期目标。 在上次议息会议上，决策者表示将依赖"更多信息的积累"来判断利率的最优水平，显示政策立场仍具灵活性。 周二即将发布的10月CPI数据，将成为市场评估美联储下一步动作的关键依据。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.summary: 美国国会民主党议员8日表示，明年1月民主党接管国会后，将对美国亿万富翁埃隆·马斯克、白宫办公厅主任斯蒂芬·米勒及部分企业发起调查。 民主党籍的联邦众议员罗伯特·加西亚与联邦参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦当天在电视访谈中作出上述表态。 △马斯克（资料图） 在民主党接管众议院后，加西亚有望担任该院监督和政府改革委员会主席。他说，调查将聚焦马斯克在“政府效率部”解雇联邦雇员一事中扮演的角色，以及米勒在特朗普政府移民执法政策中发挥的作用。加西亚称米勒是“可怕、不公正”移民政策的设计者，处于政府重大政策决策的核心，理应受到监督和调查。 沃伦还对一些企业发出警告，但并未点名具体企业。她说，靠欺骗美国家庭和投资者牟利的企业“最好准备好接受严肃调查”。 对此，美司法部长托德·布兰奇当天强硬回应，称民主党的针对性威胁“不可容忍”，并准备好应战。 △美国国会（资料图） 在3日举行的美国中期选举中，民主党从共和党手中夺回国会参众两院控制权。胜选之后，民主党将如何利用国会多数地位，成为外界关注焦点。 马斯克4日自嘲，“看来我用来介入选举的太空激光这次没起作用”。另有消息称，在此次美国中期选举周期中，马斯克已向共和党捐赠近5亿美元，成为单一选举周期内有公开记录的捐款额最多的个人。 本文来源： 央视新闻 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 历史性科技崩溃背后，是恐慌性出清还是真实的周期转折？
articles.summary: 近期全球金融市场剧烈波动，周期股与动量因子出现历史性回撤，市场对经济周期见顶的担忧急剧升温。 摩根士丹利全球固定收益研究主管Andrew Sheets认为， 当前的价格剧烈调整更可能接近一次重大不确定性的集中出清，而非经济周期终结的前兆。 在宏观层面，多项关键领先指标并未发出周期见顶信号—— 全球制造业PMI保持强势，美国收益率曲线依然正斜率，银行贷款增速在美国、欧洲及亚洲均在上行。 与此同时，美国中期选举民主党获得历史性胜利， 这一结果对债券市场而言或为利好：AI数据中心建设放缓可能拉长相关融资时间轴，能源价格下行压力也可能因此强化。 摩根士丹利维持未来6至12个月全球增长预测，预计美国经济增速超过2%，欧洲超过1%。Andrew Sheets表示，市场有可能在不确定性尚未完全消散之前就完成调整，尤其当估值修正已悄然持续一段时间之后。 周期指标未现见顶信号 Andrew Sheets指出，当前市场波动令人联想到历次经济周期末端的典型特征，但多项核心指标并不支持这一判断。 全球制造业PMI继续保持强劲，美国PMI数据近期好于预期；美国领先经济指标指数呈改善态势；美国、欧洲及亚洲的银行贷款均在扩张；信贷基本面也在持续改善。摩根士丹利跨资产团队的周期模型最新读数显示，经济仍处于健康区间。 另一项备受关注的指标——收益率曲线——同样未发出警示。无论是2年期与10年期，还是3个月与10年期利差，美国、英国、德国和日本的收益率曲线均保持正斜率。这与货币政策过度收紧、经济增长即将掉头向下的情景相悖。 Andrew Sheets表示， 历史上真正的周期大转折来临前，很少看到上述指标呈现出如此稳健的格局。 中期选举冲击AI建设预期 美国中期选举民主党取得显著胜利，翻转了众议院、参议院及多个州长职位的控制权，其中包括得克萨斯州和俄亥俄州，创下自1974年以来全国得票最强的超额表现。 选举结果引发市场对AI基础设施建设可能受到更严格监管的担忧。然而Andrew Sheets认为，这一风险虽存在，但并非基准情景，且并非新问题。 半导体股票在选举日之前已较6月峰值下跌约30%。摩根士丹利研究团队此前已多次撰文，指出电力和融资方面的瓶颈可能导致AI建设进程放缓并拉长周期。 即便在最悲观的高约束情景下——假设项目审批和电力供应均面临更大挑战——全球数据中心容量至2030年的年均复合增长率预测仍达17%。 从股票市场角度看，AI建设延迟风险需与已发生的显著估值调整相权衡。标普500指数今年以来的远期市盈率已较年初下降约19%。摩根士丹利股票策略师认为，这一调整在市场内部已悄然进行了相当长时间。 债券市场或迎来双重利好 Andrew Sheets认为，中期选举结果对债券市场的潜在正面影响更为直接。 他指出，今年困扰债券市场的两大压力源——高能源价格以及为数据中心建设融资而产生的大规模借贷——均可能因选举结果而有所缓解。 其一，AI建设节奏放缓意味着相关融资需求将分散在更长的时间维度上，单一时段市场需要消化的供给压力随之降低。 其二，据副总统万斯援引的选举分析，选民对伊朗冲突局势的不安是本次选举结果的重要因素之一。这或将促使市场下调地缘冲突再升级的风险溢价——油价目前已较10月底低约17%。 能源价格下行对欧洲尤为关键。摩根士丹利利率策略师目前青睐欧洲收益率曲线陡峭化策略。摩根士丹利新兴市场策略师也指出，油价走低将从多个维度改善新兴市场基本面。 此外，选民对通胀的普遍不满情绪，或进一步强化市场对关税措施终将证明为暂时性政策的预期。同时，更大规模的国会多数席位有望减少个别议员的阻挠空间，消除此前国会博弈带来的一项市场波动因素。 Andrew Sheets总结认为，眼下最核心的问题在于：市场正在经历的，究竟是真正的周期转折，还是正在接近重大不确定性集中出清的尾声？ 他的判断倾向于后者。周期性数据依然提供支撑，而中期选举结果可能正在消解债券市场今年面临的两项最大压力。摩根士丹利将持续用后续证据检验这一判断。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 中科星云发布“星云星座计划”，拟建“天地对等”太空算力网
articles.summary: 11月9日，2026太空云产业生态大会暨中科星云成立大会在合肥举行。中科星云太空智能科技（合肥）有限公司（以下简称"中科星云"）在会上宣布投入运营，认缴注册资本15亿元。工商登记信息显示，该公司已于11月2日完成设立登记。 作为“太空云”专项的重要产业化主体，中科星云将依托中国科学院空天信息创新研究院（以下简称"空天院"）的技术积累，整合国产算力芯片、服务器、卫星测运控、星座建设及空天信息服务等产业资源，布局太空算力基础设施，探索构建天地一体化的太空智能服务体系。 公司由中科星图、中科曙光、海光信息、星图测控、曙光数创、中科卫星6家产业主体，联合中国科学院旗下国科发展、央企诚通科创，安徽省属皖能资本、华安嘉业及省科技厅牵头主管的母基金，以及合肥产投、合肥高新创投等市、区两级投资平台，共计16家发起主体共同设立。 其背后，是空天院长期以来在空天信息领域的科研积累。此前，空天院联合国内多家科研优势单位，构建起"太空云"的概念体系、技术体制与基础平台，目标是把遥感、通信、算力三类卫星通过技术手段整合为统一调度的天基信息服务系统，推动卫星从单一功能载体向协同工作的"智能星云"演进。 大会期间，相关各方就"太空云"专项知识产权达成授权意向，会上发布"星云星座计划"。 与传统卫星主要承担数据采集、传输任务不同，太空算力的核心在于将计算能力部署到卫星及空间网络之中，使卫星具备在轨处理数据、协同计算和智能服务的能力。 6家产业发起主体中，海光信息提供国产高端算力芯片，中科曙光提供服务器整机与智算基础设施，星图测控提供卫星测运控能力，曙光数创提供算力基础设施热管理支撑，中科卫星提供感算星座建设和运营，中科星图贯通空天数据与信息服务，覆盖了天基信息服务从芯片到应用的完整领域。 在此基础上，中科星云将坚持全栈国产化自主技术路线，重点布局太空算力芯片、太空计算机、星间高速互联及天地资源调度平台等关键领域，探索形成自主可控的技术体系与标准。 在技术发展方向上，中科星云提出建设和运营"天地对等"的太空算力网。 所谓"天地对等"，并不是简单追求太空算力规模与地面算力完全相同，而是希望太空算力能够在规模、价格和应用层面与地面算力实现对等协同，使太空成为与地面算力网络地位同等、能力互补、统一调度的信息网络节点。 为实现这一目标，公司提出沿着"感算、通算、超算"三个阶段逐步推进。 第一阶段感算融合，卫星在采集数据的同时完成处理，实现"边采边算、即拍即算"。第二阶段通算融合，依托星间高速互联与在轨组网计算，支撑巨型遥感星座协同运行。第三阶段超算协同，汇聚在轨算力构建轨道数据中心，形成"通感算用"一体化、天地统一调度的太空算力网络。 从单颗卫星的感知计算，到多颗卫星之间的协同组网，再到大规模在轨算力资源的统一调度，这一路径体现了太空算力从单点能力建设走向系统级基础设施建设的技术演进方向。 除了技术和基础设施建设，中科星云也将着力构建开放协同的产业运营体系。 公司提出依托三大核心生态推动产业发展。一是深度融入空天院牵头建设的"太空云"生态，联合科研机构、航天企业及高校，推动感知、通信、计算、智能一体化的天基信息服务体系建设。二是计划借助中科曙光与海光信息的运营生态，探索将地面智算基础设施和国产算力芯片的运营能力向太空延伸，建立天地一体的算力运营体系。三是联合产业链上下游企业，共同建设和运营星云太空基础设施，形成开放、协同、可持续的产业发展模式。 中科星云选择落地合肥，也与当地近年来在商业航天及硬科技领域的持续布局密切相关。 在新能源汽车、集成电路、新型显示等领域形成产业集群后，合肥正进一步向空天信息和商业航天领域延伸，推动产业资源从卫星数据应用向卫星制造、大规模卫星运营等更上游环节拓展。 目前，合肥已形成涵盖卫星制造、卫星运营、卫星数据应用等环节的产业基础。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 对标2000 与 2008：本轮 4.1 万亿AI 债务裂痕有多深？
articles.summary: 近期，随着美股科技巨头财报陆续披露，市场担忧的焦点已从此前的AI盈利预期与资本开支回报，进一步转向AI债务融资能力。随着AI产业继续以史无前例的速度扩张，AI巨头资产负债表所体现的债务水平仅是其债务总额的冰山一角；真正隐藏在水面之下的，是庞大且盘根错节的表外债务。 截至目前，包括Alphabet、Meta、微软、亚马逊、SpaceX、英伟达、博通及甲骨文在内的8家AI综合体，其表外承诺总额已攀升至4.11万亿美元。这一数字较Q2末3.12万亿美元激增近万亿美元。其中，长期采购承诺约2.25万亿美元，尚未开始的租赁约1.39万亿美元，担保及备用信贷约2730亿美元。 当前AI综合体在资产负债表中实际报告的金融债务与租赁负债合计约为1万亿美元。这意味着AI综合体每1美元表内债务和租赁背后，对应超过4美元的表外承诺。 现阶段科技巨头CDS持续飙升，甲骨文5年期CDS一度触及343个基点的历史峰值，高评级科技债券收益率升至两位数，AI融资环境显著恶化。面对4.1万亿美元表外承诺与日益收紧的信贷环境，这一局面令人回想起2008年金融危机前对次贷规模的低估及其灾难性后果。若市场持续低估AI表外承诺所蕴含的结构性债务矛盾，是否也将低估由此衍生的系统性风险？ 两轮历史大对标：AI债务与2008次贷、2000互联网泡沫
